definition: A part of a whole, written $\frac{a}{b}$: the denominator $b$ (never $0$) is how many equal parts the whole is split into, and the numerator $a$ is how many of them you take.
A fraction whose numerator is smaller than its denominator, such as $\frac{3}{5}$, so it is worth less than $1$.
A fraction whose numerator is equal to or bigger than its denominator, such as $\frac{7}{4}$, so it is worth $1$ or more and can be written as a whole or mixed number.
A whole number and a proper fraction written together, such as $2\frac{1}{3}$, which means $2 + \frac{1}{3}$.
An amount out of $100$, written with the % sign, so $35\%$ means $\frac{35}{100}$ or $0.35$.
A fraction with the same value as another but different numbers, such as $\frac{8}{12}$ and $\frac{2}{3}$, made by multiplying or dividing the numerator and denominator by the same non-zero number.

A decimal in which one digit or a block of digits repeats forever, such as $0.4\dot{1} = 0.4111\ldots$; dots over the first and last digits of the block (or a bar over the whole block) show what repeats.
